judgment.reasoning_summary: The problem involves two runners moving in opposite directions on a circular track. The key is to find the time when they both return to the starting point simultaneously for the second time. Since they are running in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds. The time to meet at the starting point is the least common multiple (LCM) of the time it takes each to complete one lap. The LCM of 10 minutes (Alice's lap time) and 15 minutes (Bob's lap time) is 30 minutes. Therefore, they will meet at the starting point every 30 minutes. The second meeting occurs at 60 minutes.
